html:
Meru is the name the map gives to Aboriginal peoples of the Riverland in South Australia, along the Murray River between the Victorian border and the river's great bend.

The name has been used for a wider grouping that took in peoples such as the Ngaiawang, the Ngawait and the Erawirung, whose languages belonged to the Lower Murray group. The river and its lagoons gave fish, mussels, waterbirds and reeds. Neighbours on the map include the Ngarrindjeri downriver, the Ngadjuri to the west and the Danggali to the north.

Overlanders drove cattle and sheep along the Murray to Adelaide from 1838, and violent clashes followed. Several of these peoples are now considered gone as separate groups. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: Meru is the name the map gives to Aboriginal peoples of the Riverland in South Australia, along the Murray River between the Victorian border and the river's great bend.
